title: Hopscotch prefetch and read-hedging to cut tail latency for sparse dashboard filters
creator: Sana Patel
description: Background: Certain console dashboards that expose sparse, high-cardinality filters (eg. by tenant tag, feature flag, or trace id) exhibit long tail p99 latency due to read fanout and cold index lookups. This ticket implements a multi-pronged server-side approach that reduces tail latency without excessively increasing backend IOPS or cache memory. Goal: reduce p99 query latency for sparse filters by 3x and bring 95th percentile under 300ms for typical single-route dashboard queries while keeping overall read amplification <1.5x.
proposed_solution: Introduce a lightweight hopscotch index — a compact, cache-friendly bloom+bucket map keyed by (tenant, indexed-field-prefix) that points to candidate shard buckets to avoid full inverted-index scans.
Add a TTL-driven prefetch layer: when a hopscotch lookup indicates likely matches, enqueue async prefetches for small hot shards with time-decayed priority to prevent rework on near-term queries.
Forward cursor augmentation for pagination: attach a small token containing hopscotch hints to cursor payloads so subsequent pages avoid re-evaluating expensive filters.
Read hedging policy: for requests with expected high tail risk, issue a concurrent read to a best-effort cache replica after a 12ms microdelay (configurable) and use whichever responds first.
Server-side per-tenant budget controller: limit prefetch parallelism per tenant to avoid noisy-neighbor amplification and surface metrics when limits are hit.
Compatibility path: fall back to existing inverted-index path if hopscotch index miss or during rollout; index building is online and incremental.
Benchmarks & safety: measure additional IOPS and cache residency; cap prefetch window size and evict oldest prefetch entries under pressure.
rollout_plan: Phase 0 (canary): deploy hopscotch index and forward cursor in internal staging for 48h against synthetic workloads; verify correctness and no query regressions.
Phase 1 (10% tenant sample): enable prefetch with conservative TTL and per-tenant budget; monitor p50/p95/p99 and cache hit ratios for 7 days.
Phase 2 (50%): increase prefetch window and enable read-hedging for queries flagged as high-risk; adjust hedging microdelay based on latency distribution.
Phase 3 (global): enable by default with automatic backoff when cluster-wide IOPS or memory pressure detected; ship config knobs in console.
Rollback: on regression >15% increase in P95 or unexpected IOPS spike, revert prefetch and hedging while keeping hopscotch index read-only mode.
Migration: backfill hopscotch index incrementally using existing index scans during low-traffic windows; track progress via metric.
success_metrics: Reduce p99 for sparse-filter dashboard queries by 3x (baseline p99 ~1200ms -> target <400ms).
Reduce p95 to <300ms for sampled production queries under 99th percentile load.
Keep average read amplification <=1.5x and additional IOPS budget for prefetching <20% of current read IOPS.
Cache hit improvement of +12% on hopscotch-indexed keys for the sampled tenants.
No correctness regressions (results identical to current path) for 100% of test vectors.
telemetry: New metrics: hopscotch_lookup_latency_ms, hopscotch_miss_rate, prefetch_enqueue_rate, prefetch_eviction_rate, hedged_read_win_rate, per_tenant_prefetch_tokens.
Dashboards: prefetch cost vs latency saved, per-tenant budget saturation, p50/p95/p99 before vs after hedging, read amplification heatmap by tenant.
Traces: attach hopscotch hint IDs to existing request traces for tail-sampling analysis.
Alerts: p99 > 500ms for 5m or prefetch_eviction_rate > 5% sustained triggers on-call paging.
